title: model-catalog: add capability flags, pricing & filters to /models endpoints
author: Aisha Patel
commits: Add capability flags and pricing fields to model registry schema
Expose new fields on GET /v1/models and add query filters
Map capability flags into OpenAI-compat layer responses
Update TS/Python SDK types and docs
Add unit and integration tests for filters and compatibility mapping
description: Motivation: downstream clients (console, SDKs, internal routing) need richer model metadata to make routing and UI decisions. This PR extends the model catalog with explicit capability flags (streaming, function_calling, structured_output, openai_compat), numeric limits/pricing fields (max_input_tokens, max_output_tokens, price_per_1k_tokens_usd, qps_limit, regional_limits) and adds server-side filters to the GET /v1/models endpoint. Summary: - Model registry schema extended with capability booleans and pricing/limits fields. - GET /v1/models now accepts query parameters: capabilities (comma-separated), min_max_output_tokens, region, openai_compat (boolean), price_max_usd. - Response includes a new top-level capabilities array and pricing object (flat fields are also kept for backward compatibility). - OpenAI compatibility layer now maps these fields to ensure the openai-compat endpoint can return compatible model metadata and filter by openai_compatible models when requested. - SDKs (TS/Python) updated to surface the new fields. Backwards compatibility: default behavior is unchanged when no new fields/filters are used; new fields are optional in the JSON. Migration: lightweight DB migration adds nullable columns, indexed capability flags for fast filtering. Testing: unit tests for schema, integration tests for filter combinations and openai-compat mapping, and end-to-end smoke test in perf-canary. Checklist: [x] schema migration [x] handler changes [x] SDK updates [x] docs updated [x] tests added [x] perf smoke. Related: ENG-1023 (catalog filtering), PM-214 (dataset of capability needs).
review_comments: Miguel Ortega: Can we standardize the field name to openai_compatible instead of openai_compat? It reads clearer from the SDK side.

Aisha Patel: We discussed in PR thread; kept openai_compat for brevity in wire format but added openai_compatible as an alias in the SDKs and docs. Added a note in docs/api/models.md explaining both names.
Sarah Li: Filter semantics look good. Please ensure capability filtering is AND semantics by default and provide OR via separate parameter. Tests should cover both cases.
Aisha Patel: Implemented capabilities=streaming,function_calling as AND semantics and added capabilities_or=true to enable OR semantics. Tests added for both.
Jonah Reed: Concern: price_per_1k_tokens_usd as a float in the DB could cause precision issues. Consider storing as integer micros (USD * 1e6).
Aisha Patel: Switched storage to price_per_microunits (integer) and kept price_per_1k_tokens_usd in API responses for readability. Migration script updated.
release_notes: Added model catalog capability flags and pricing/limits to /v1/models. New query filters: capabilities, min_max_output_tokens, region, openai_compat, price_max_usd. SDKs updated. Backwards compatible; no breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: DB migration adds nullable columns and indexes on capability flags; migration runs in <1 min on typical catalog size. Rolling deploy recommended: migrate schema first, then deploy services. Monitor catalog_metrics.models_filter_latency and metrics around registry DB.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for schema encoding/decoding and SDK types. Integration tests cover combinations of capability filters, price filters and openai_compat flag. Perf smoke shows negligible latency impact for indexed flags. CI run: all checks passed after a single rerun of integration tests.
api_examples: Response: { id: "redwood/fast-encoder", name: "Fast Encoder", capabilities: ["streaming", "structured_output"], max_input_tokens: 2048, max_output_tokens: 1024, price_per_1k_tokens_usd: 0.40 }
OpenAI-compat: GET /v1/openai/models?openai_compat=true will now prefer models with openai_compat flag set and expose mapped limits in the openai model object.
